A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedFACT research and provide readable main text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Relocated material and the added checklist can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on Compas, Adult, CelebA, and ENEM, including comparative results, multiclass evaluation, sensitivity analyses, and scalability studies.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports revised numerical results, particularly for ENEM.

M1.justification: The personalized cost-sensitive training, model ensembling, and bi-level post-processing procedures remain substantively unchanged. Notation edits and the added discussion of representable fairness constraints do not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four datasets, including the same CelebA four-class and ENEM five-class tasks and sensitive groups. Heterogeneity and client-count scenarios are retained; no additional dataset or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain FedAvg, FairFed, FedFB, FCFL, praFFL/praFFed, and Cost. The Pareto plots retain their respective comparator sets, and multiclass comparisons remain limited to FedAvg and FedFACT variants. LoGoFair remains discussed but unevaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix D.1 change the reported binary fairness evaluation from EO to EOP, accompanied by changed plot labels. This is a reported metric revision, although retained Equalized Odds wording and EO formulas leave actual recomputation unclear. Dataset splits, client counts, models, and hyperparameter ranges remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The ensemble-size analysis in Table 6 and client-count scalability analysis in Figure 5 contain revised ENEM evidence. Their tested questions, parameter sweeps, and qualitative conclusions remain unchanged. The multiclass analysis moved into Section 5.2 already appeared in v1.

E5.justification: Both Table 2 footnotes report averages of five repeated experiments. V2 adds no seeds, defined error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Its new checklist assertion about statistical significance supplies no additional uncertainty estimates or procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 extensively replaces ENEM results. At gamma = 0.5, joint post-processing changes from (71.21, 0.0056, 0.0198) to (66.52, 0.0162, 0.0184) for accuracy, global disparity, and local disparity. Under the heterogeneous split, the highest fair-method accuracy shifts from joint to local-only post-processing. ENEM results in Table 6 and Pareto/scalability plots also change. These are revised reported outcomes, not demonstrated improvements from a changed method.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 introduces mathematical conditions for expressing ratio-based fairness constraints as linear constraints when the denominator has a fixed sign, with a calibration-within-groups example. The central Bayes-optimality, convergence, and generalization results and proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: controllable global/local fairness, multiclass applicability, Bayes-optimal characterization, and theoretically supported in-processing and post-processing algorithms. Revised wording and results do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 replaces v1's suggestion of joint deployment with an explicit warning that combining the two stages lacks theoretical justification because the in-processing classifier need not estimate Bayes scores. Appendix A.3 adds applicability conditions for ratio-based fairness. The small-local-sample limitation and multiclass interpretation were already present in v1.

D1.justification: V2 adds a reproducibility statement identifying a code repository and checklist statements that code accompanies the supplemental material. These are new access disclosures; repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Existing dataset preparation, hyperparameter ranges, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 84 to 97 entries, adding fairness and application references, including support for the calibration-within-groups discussion. Section 2 and the substantive comparison with LoGoFair in Appendix C.2 remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose and notation edits, revises author/header information, adds reproducibility and acknowledgment sections and a NeurIPS checklist, and moves the multiclass discussion into the main text. The scientific narrative and section organization otherwise remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V1's multiclass Figure 3 becomes main-text Figure 1 without changing its plots. Binary Pareto figures are renumbered, fairness-axis labels change, and ENEM panels receive revised scales and curves. Tables retain their structures, and appendix figures reflow; no new figure or table is introduced.

improvement.justification: The code-access disclosure, ratio-constraint discussion, and warning against combining calibration stages improve documentation and clarify applicability. However, v2 introduces conflicting EO/EOP labeling and replaces substantial ENEM results without explaining the revisions under the retained experimental settings. The PDFs do not establish whether those replacements correct earlier errors or reflect undocumented changes. These competing effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
